title: Bind configuration lists with the right element type

blocks.text: The gateway reads its configuration into plain settings objects: a line such as `listenPorts=8443,9443` fills the list field `listenPorts`. A release that bound a fresh `GatewaySettings` started fine and then failed on the first connection with a `ClassCastException` in code that reads `int port = settings.listenPorts.get(0)`.

`SettingsBinder` already finds the field, clears the list and converts each item. Finish `elementType(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/SettingsBinder.java`: the type every item of that field's list must have.

Settings classes declare their lists as `List<Something>`, or as a named class of their own such as `class PortList extends ArrayList<Integer>`, and a list may be empty before binding. When you're done, every item ends up as the declared element type in all of these cases. About four lines in total.

cases.says: items bound into a List<String> field are the trimmed strings
items bound into a List<Long> field that holds defaults replace them as Longs
items bound into an empty List<Integer> field become Integers, though the list holds nothing to inspect
items bound into a field declared as a class extending ArrayList<Integer> become Integers

origin.section: Type Arguments Survive in Declarations, Not in Objects

concepts: A class that extends a parameterized type keeps the type argument in its superclass signature, which getGenericSuperclass() reads back.
Type arguments are kept in the generic signatures of fields, methods and classes and read with getGenericType() and its relatives, so a binder learns a list's element type from the declaration.
